already_flagged: OQ-06: Can employees pick from a fixed list of countries or from all countries? (AC-01.2.2 says no country is excluded until this is decided.)

questions.question: AC-01.1.1 says the employee is asked for street, house number, postcode and town, "whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad". Does that mean we ask a separate question 'within Switzerland or abroad?', or only that the four parts are required in both cases? US-01.2 and AC-01.2.3 work out Swiss or abroad from the country. A separate question would duplicate that, and the two answers could disagree.

The house number is 'required always', but the Notes say the meeting never discussed addresses without one, and the trace check says no source supports 'cannot be completed while any is missing'. Can an employee finish the report if their address has no house number (rural addresses, named buildings, many foreign addresses)? Or with no postcode, in a country that doesn't use postcodes? If yes, what do they enter instead?

Should the new address be checked for plausibility, for example a Swiss postcode that has 4 digits and matches the town, or postcode formats for other countries? Or is any text accepted as long as each part is filled in? Nothing in the spec says what makes an address 'given' rather than just non-empty.

AC-01.2.3 says HR 'can see whether the move is within Switzerland or abroad'. For employees who already live abroad (cross-border staff), does a move inside their country, or a move into Switzerland, count as abroad? OQ-04 covers this in open-questions.md and lists 'Country of the new address' as affected, but this feature only links OQ-06.

AC-01.1.2 and AC-01.2.3 only say HR 'looks at the report' and 'can update the master data'. Is HR told when a new report comes in, or does HR check for reports itself? Is updating master data a manual HR step, or does the report change the employee record directly? This decides whether we build a notification or an integration.

How should the employee enter the country if they type it, or if the source of the country names is open? For example, if they type 'Schweiz', 'Suisse' or 'Deutschland', should it be turned into the English name? G-02 sets English names, but AC-01.2.2 doesn't say what happens to non-English input.

Are address extras such as c/o, apartment or floor, a second address line, or a PO box allowed or needed? The address is defined as exactly five parts, but documents sent to the wrong recipient line could still go astray.
Is Liechtenstein treated as abroad? It uses Swiss postcodes but is a different country, and that affects payroll (source tax) and the canton logic that depend on this feature.
Can an employee correct or withdraw a report after completing it, for example after a typo in the postcode? Can HR send it back? The spec only covers a first, complete report.
Should we stop or warn when the new address is the same as the address HR already has on record?
AC-01.1.3 says the reason for the move must never be asked. Does that also rule out a free-text comment or notes field, where employees could write their reason without being asked?

Does the employee always fill in the report, or can HR enter a move for an employee (for example one reported by phone or letter)? The stakeholders list both, but every AC starts with 'an employee reports'.

tech_leaks.quote: the report cannot be completed while any of these four is missing
tech_leaks.why: This blocks the employee from finishing the report. The spec's own trace check says no source supports it. It is invented system behaviour, not a stakeholder requirement: HR only said what it needs, not that incomplete reports must be blocked.

tech_leaks.quote: Whether employees choose from a fixed list of countries or from all countries is still open (see OQ-06)
tech_leaks.why: Calling it 'choose from a list' assumes a picker-style control. The business question is only which countries are allowed; how the country is entered is up to engineering.
